answer:
**Answer**

The Nordic country/UK that experienced the largest percentage rise in annual CO₂ emissions between the Kyoto Protocol (1997) and the Paris Agreement (2015) is **Iceland**.

**Evidence & calculation**

| Country | 1997 emissions (t) | 2015 emissions (t) | % increase |
|---------|--------------------|--------------------|------------|
| Denmark | 3 232 863 | 4 578 364 | 41.7 % |
| Finland | 739 173 | 1 367 664 | 85.0 % |
| Iceland | 19 032 | 66 812 | **≈ 251 %** |
| Norway | 89 900 | 163 465 | 81.8 % |
| Sweden | 278 370 | 540 822 | 94.3 % |
| United Kingdom | 339 429 | 431 650 | 27.2 % |

From the Our World in Data CSV “Annual CO₂ emissions per country” the 1997 and 2015 values were taken for each country; the percentage increase was calculated as  
\((2015 - 1997) / 1997 \times 100\).  
Iceland’s growth of ≈ 251 % is higher than any other country in the group.  

*Source:* Our World in Data, “Annual CO₂ emissions per country” (CSV).

steps.text:
**Highest percentage increase in annual CO₂ emissions (1997 → 2015)**  

| Country | 1997 emissions (t) | 2015 emissions (t) | Percentage increase |
|---------|--------------------|--------------------|---------------------|
| Denmark | 3,232,863 | 4,578,364 | **≈ 41.7 %** |
| Finland | 739,173 | 1,367,664 | **≈ 85.0 %** |
| Iceland | 19,032 | 66,812 | **≈ 251.1 %** |
| Norway | 89,900 | 163,465 | **≈ 81.8 %** |
| Sweden | 278,370 | 540,822 | **≈ 94.3 %** |
| United Kingdom | 339,429 | 431,650 | **≈ 27.2 %** |

**Answer – Iceland** has the largest percentage increase, rising about **251 %** from 1997 (the Kyoto Protocol adoption year) to 2015 (the Paris Agreement adoption year).

---

### How the figure was calculated

From the “Annual CO₂ emissions per country” CSV of Our World in Data:

```
Denmark,DNK,1997,3232863
Denmark,DNK,2015,4578364
Finland,FIN,1997,739173
Finland,FIN,2015,1367664
Iceland,ISL,1997,19032
Iceland,ISL,2015,66812
Norway,NOR,1997,89900
Norway,NOR,2015,163465
Sweden,SWE,1997,278370
Sweden,SWE,2015,540822
United Kingdom,GBR,1997,339429
United Kingdom,GBR,2015,431650
```

The percentage increase is computed as  

\[
\frac{\text{2015 value} - \text{1997 value}}{\text{1997 value}}\times100
\]

Iceland’s increase equals  
\[
\frac{66,812-19,032}{19,032}\times100 \approx 251.1\%
\]

which is higher than all the other Nordic countries and the UK.

Our World in Data, “Annual CO₂ emissions per country” (CSV file).  Data lines for 1997 and 2015 are shown above.
